source_of_truth: Reading app/composables/useAuth.ts: the login response's tokens are persisted in web storage through two syntactic variants of the same defect - sessionStorage.setItem('refresh_token', data.refreshToken) and the VueUse useLocalStorage('auth_token') wrapper later assigned the access token. Both put a readable credential in web storage rather than an HttpOnly cookie. A correct auditor must flag token-in-web-storage for BOTH variants at confirmed (token-like key names; the refresh value comes from a response field).

expected.rationale: useLocalStorage('auth_token') wrapper persists a token-like key in localStorage; a credential in web storage is XSS-readable.
sessionStorage.setItem('refresh_token', data.refreshToken): token-like key, response-sourced value, written to web storage instead of an HttpOnly cookie.
